title: The Vernacular Press Act, 1878

endcard.line: Pictures: Yercaud-elango (CC BY 4.0); unknown photographer (public domain)

anim.title: 14 March 1878
items: Aimed at papers in Indian languages

segments.say: On the fourteenth of March eighteen seventy-eight, a new law took aim at newspapers printed in Indian languages.
The Vernacular Press Act was meant to silence those who criticised the government. It covered publications in Indian languages, but left English-language papers alone.
It was proposed by the Viceroy, Lord Lytton, whose government faced anger over its policies, including a grand Delhi Durbar held while India suffered a severe famine.
The same criticism in English was left alone. Many saw the law as plain discrimination against the Indian press.

anim.title: A quick escape
items: Turned itself into an English weekly
Within a week of the Act

segments.say: One Calcutta paper, the Amrita Bazar Patrika, slipped out of the law's reach by becoming an all-English weekly within a week.

items.text: Arms Act and Vernacular Press Act

segments.say: The same year also brought the Arms Act, which stopped Indians from keeping arms. The Press Act was withdrawn in eighteen eighty-one, under Lord Ripon.
For GS One, pair eighteen seventy-eight with Lytton, and eighteen eighty-one with Ripon's repeal.

sources: NCERT Class 8, Our Pasts III, ch. 8 'The Making of the National Movement' (hess208, read): the Arms Act was passed in 1878, disallowing Indians from possessing arms; in the same year the Vernacular Press Act was enacted to silence those critical of the government

Wikipedia, 'Vernacular Press Act' (read): proposed by Viceroy Lytton and passed by the Viceroy's Council on 14 March 1878; excluded English-language publications; public opinion against Lytton's policies such as the Delhi Durbar (1877) during a severe famine; Amrita Bazar Patrika converted to an all-English weekly within a week; minor modification in October 1878; withdrawn by Lord Ripon's administration in 1881

quiz.q: Which Viceroy proposed the Vernacular Press Act?
quiz.why: Lytton proposed it; Ripon's government withdrew it in 1881.

quiz.q: Which papers did the Vernacular Press Act leave out?
quiz.why: It covered publications in Indian languages only.

quiz.q: Which other law was passed in 1878?
quiz.why: NCERT: the Arms Act was passed in 1878.

reviewNote: The 1878 Arms Act and the Act's purpose are from NCERT Class 8; the details (Lytton, 14 March, Amrita Bazar Patrika, 1881 repeal by Ripon) are from Wikipedia and should be checked against NCERT Class 12 or a National Archives source before approval. The printing press is a museum piece, used as a period object; it isn't claimed to be from 1878. Moving facts: none.
